transcript.content: Thank you for calling Summit Air. How can I help you today?
Hi, quick question first, why does my radiator bang?

Banging radiators usually happen when water condenses and gets pushed through the pipes as the heat comes on, or when the pipes expand and rub against brackets. It's common in older steam or hot-water systems. If it's happening often, or it's loud or getting worse, a technician can take a look and tell you what's going on. Would you like me to set up a visit?
Okay, that makes sense. Before I book anything, what's short cycling? The boiler keeps turning on and off a lot, and I'm wondering if that's related.

Short cycling means the boiler or furnace turns on and off in quick bursts instead of running steady cycles to heat the home. It can come from a dirty filter, a sensor problem, an oversized unit, or low airflow or water pressure. It isn't the same as banging pipes, though it can make the system work harder and wear out sooner. A technician can find the actual cause. Would you like to set up a visit?

Okay, that helps. Yes, I'd like someone to come take a look. Do you have anything available this week? I'm home most of the day, and I can approve repairs if they're needed. There's no gate code or pets, so the tech can come right in.
I can set that up. Can I get your name?
Jamie Ortiz.
Thanks. And this is for a residential property, right? Like a home or an apartment?
Yes, it's a house in Astoria. 25-30 30th Rd, Astoria, 11102. I'm calling from 678 555 0272.
